kurz: Why, of the two risks in a share price, only market risk is rewarded, and how the other can be eliminated free of charge through diversification.

bloecke.md:
A share price moves for two reasons. The first reason affects only this one company, for example falsified accounts, a lost patent dispute or a production outage at a plant. The second reason affects all companies, for example a turn in the interest rate cycle, a war or a recession. Risk of the first kind is called **unsystematic** or idiosyncratic risk, and risk of the second kind **systematic risk** or market risk.

This distinction determines which risk investors are rewarded for. In June 2020, Wirecard was a member of the DAX, and a few days later it was insolvent. Investors who held only this share lost almost everything, while the index moved within its usual range during those days. In 2022, by contrast, equities and bonds fell at the same time because central banks raised interest rates to fight inflation. No security could escape this rise in interest rates.

Unsystematic risk can be eliminated through diversification; systematic risk cannot. That is why the market pays no premium for unsystematic risk. Investors who hold individual securities therefore bear a risk for which they are not compensated. The saying about the “only free lunch” on the stock market, attributed to Harry Markowitz, simply means that diversification lowers risk without the expected return falling along with it.

bloecke.erklaerung: Variance of an equally weighted portfolio of n securities. The first term tends towards zero as n grows; the second remains.
variablen: mean variance of the individual securities
mean covariance of all pairs of securities
bloecke.beispiel: For very large n, only the average covariance remains. It forms the lower limit of portfolio risk, that is, the systematic risk that no number of securities can push below.

bloecke.md:
Two statements follow from the formula. First, each security's own contribution to portfolio risk decreases with 1/n, that is, very quickly. Second, the remaining risk depends on how strongly the securities move together, not on the number of positions. A portfolio of 200 shares that all depend on the same business cycle therefore has many positions but is poorly diversified.

Elton and Gruber calculated how quickly the first effect works using 3,290 US shares. On average, a single security had a volatility of 49.2% a year. With ten equally weighted securities, it was only 23.9%, with thirty 20.9% and with a thousand 19.2%. The last 970 securities therefore reduce volatility less than the step from one security to two.

bloecke.titel: Portfolio volatility by number of securities
bloecke.unter: Equally weighted US equity portfolios, standard deviation of annual returns (Elton/Gruber, 3,290 securities). The dashed line shows the value for 1,000 securities, which the curve never falls below.

bloecke.md: This curve is the origin of the widespread claim that a portfolio is diversified from ten or fifteen shares upwards. The impression is misleading, because the eye compares standard deviations, while risk is made up of variances. With ten securities, the standard deviation is only 25% above the lower limit. Of the variance, however, just over a third is still unsystematic, that is, risk without reward. Only at around fifty securities does this share fall into single digits.

bloecke.titel: Share of unrewarded specific risk in the variance
bloecke.unter: Own calculation from the same Elton/Gruber figures: (variance minus variance at 1,000 securities) divided by variance. Where the standard deviation curve is already flat, this share is still clearly present.

bloecke.md: William Bernstein compared 98 randomly drawn portfolios of 15 shares each with the equally weighted S&P 500 over ten years. The volatility of these portfolios was unremarkable, but their results deviated markedly from the market. Three quarters lagged behind the market, some by 5 to 10 percentage points a year. The reason is the right skew of share returns. A few securities deliver most of the gains, and portfolios without these securities lag the market persistently despite normal volatility. The dispersion of terminal wealth is therefore more meaningful than the standard deviation.

bloecke.unter: Period December 1989 to November 1999, compared with the equally weighted S&P 500 (24.15% a year). The fact that most of these portfolios lag the market is due to the skewed distribution and not to chance.

bloecke.md:
## Five axes of diversification with unequal benefits

Diversifying across many securities is the first and cheapest step, and today it is available for a few basis points through an index fund. However, it only eliminates the risk of individual companies.

As for industries, 25 securities from just two sectors do not achieve the risk reduction shown by the curve above. Ready-made indices are not neutral here either. At the end of August 2026, information technology accounted for 29.8% of the MSCI World. A technology fund alongside such an index fund therefore increases an industry weighting that is already high.

Individual country markets can go whole decades without any gain in value. After their peak at the end of 1989, Japanese shares took more than three decades to return to their old index level. US shares returned minus 0.8% a year in real terms from 1966 to 1981, and minus 0.8% again from 2000 to 2012. In the 21 countries with a continuous history since 1900, equities did outperform bonds, the money market and inflation everywhere. But this did not hold in every decade, and the lead was not equally large in every country.

Diversification across asset classes has the greatest additional effect, because the various equity segments are almost all closely linked. Calculated in US dollars, the correlation of US large caps with shares from other developed markets from 2008 to 2026 was 0.87, with emerging markets 0.76 and with real estate shares 0.75. Corporate bonds came to 0.45, gold to 0.08 and long-term government bonds to minus 0.07. Regional diversification therefore barely reduces volatility, but it does avoid concentrations in individual countries. Lower volatility can only be achieved with other asset classes. The next lesson covers how strong this effect is mathematically.

For diversification over time, there are data on the MSCI World in euros. Between 1970 and 2025, it was positive in all 42 rolling 15-year windows, at 1.8% a year in the worst one. Over ten years, 5 of 47 windows were still negative. The probability of a loss therefore falls with the investment horizon, but the possible size of the loss in euros does not. Time is therefore a weaker form of diversification than prospectuses make it appear.

punkte: Different sources of risk such as global equities, government bonds of good credit quality and cash

bloecke.md:
## Unequal weighting in world ETFs

Broad indices reflect whatever concentration the market has at any given time. This is not a flaw in the index construction. But you should know about it before taking such a fund to be a picture of the world economy.

bloecke.md: Spreading money across several fund providers protects against a risk that legally hardly exists. The fund assets are kept separate from the assets of the management company. For German funds set up as segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen), the fund assets do not form part of the insolvency estate if the fund management company (KVG) becomes insolvent (Section 99(3) KAGB, German Investment Code). For foreign funds, for example from Ireland or Luxembourg, the law of the country of domicile applies. The overlap in holdings, on the other hand, remains even with several providers. With instant-access savings accounts, conversely, protection is limited in amount, because statutory deposit protection covers up to €100,000 per customer and institution.

In Germany, diversification also has a tax side. Under the Investment Tax Act (InvStG), an equity fund receives a **partial exemption** (Teilfreistellung) of 30%; an individual share does not. For the same gross return, more is therefore left over net from the fund.

Exiting a concentrated position, on the other hand, incurs one-off costs. The realised gain is subject to 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus the solidarity surcharge, 26.375% in total, or around 28% with church tax. The saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 (€2,000 for joint assessment) makes only a first part of the gain tax-free. Investors reducing a large position that was inherited or built up through employee share schemes therefore usually spread the sale over several years. The most favourable split can be calculated.

Correlations are not fixed quantities. In periods of stress, risky assets increasingly move together, so diversification works least well in exactly the phases when it is needed most. During the financial crisis, the MSCI World in euros at one stage lost 53.4% (peak in June 2007 to trough in March 2009), and the MSCI Emerging Markets 59.8%. Regional diversification was of practically no help. For such phases, you should assume correlations close to one for risky assets. Then only the allocation helps, that is, the share of wealth that is held in risky assets at all. A larger number of securities does not change this.

Diversification lowers risk and is not a return strategy. It eliminates the risk for which there is no premium and leaves the risk for which there is one. That is why it is free, but also limited. Risk lower than market risk can only be achieved with a smaller share of risky assets.

mitnehmen: Only systematic risk is rewarded; the risk of individual securities earns no premium and can be eliminated free of charge through diversification.
With ten securities, the standard deviation falls to 24%, but around a third of the variance remains unsystematic; only from about 50 securities does this remainder become small.
Low volatility does not automatically mean low risk, because in Bernstein's simulation three quarters of the 15-share portfolios lagged behind the market.
Diversifying across securities and industries is quick, diversifying across countries avoids concentrations, and only other asset classes bring a marked reduction in volatility.
A world ETF is broad but unevenly diversified: at the end of August 2026, 72% was in the USA and 30% in the IT sector.

begriffe.text: Risk that affects only individual companies or industries. It can be eliminated through diversification and is therefore not rewarded with a risk premium.
Market risk that affects all securities together. It remains even in the broadest portfolio and is the part of risk for which there is a premium.
Excessive dependence on a single source, such as one security, one industry, one country or your own employer.
Many positions carrying the same risks, for example several funds with the same heavyweights or individual shares from one industry.
Share of income exempted from tax under the Investment Tax Act (InvStG). For private assets, it is 30% for equity funds and 15% for mixed funds.
